rows.subtype: Approach: freeze and film the scene instead of helping [Pitfall]
rows.description: Shock and habit lead the person to record video while the injured person waits. Nobody calls for help for several minutes, showing how the bystander effect delays action.

rows.description: The person points at people and says: you call 112, you stop traffic, you bring water and a blanket. Clear roles overcome the diffusion of responsibility.

rows.subtype: Approach: when involved, exchange details and document the scene [Action]
rows.description: After a minor collision, the driver checks that everyone is unhurt, takes photos, notes the number plate and insurer, and informs the police if needed. Calm documentation helps later claims without arguing.

rows.subtype: Approach: argue over blame at the roadside [Pitfall]
rows.description: Both drivers shout about fault while an injured cyclist lies aside. Emotion and defensiveness delay care and a crowd gathers, so the priority of injured people is forgotten.

rows.subtype: Approach: seek support and review habits afterwards [Revision]
rows.description: Shaken after the event, the person talks with family, sees a doctor for lingering symptoms, and decides to follow stricter rules on helmets, speed and night riding. Learning from the event changes future routines.
